&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; shutdown (BSD version) - Shut down the UNIX system &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Std input: Not used &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Std output: Not used &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; SEE ALSO &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ![sarrow.gif](content/ad91af06ad96c57f0a338bded4c42f0e.gif)*For more information, see page 300* &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Notes: Requires root privilege &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Useful options: &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; -h means halt the system. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; -r means shut down and reboot. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; now means dont wait to shut down. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; +MIN means wait MIN minutes before shutting down. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; shutdown (System V version) - Shut down the UNIX system &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Std input: Not used &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Std output: Not used &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; SEE ALSO &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ![sarrow.gif](content/ad91af06ad96c57f0a338bded4c42f0e.gif)*For more information, see page 300* &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Notes: Requires root privilege &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Useful options: &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; -g MIN means broadcast warning and wait MIN minutes grace period before shutdown. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;

&#124; Page 790 &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; -i STATE means go to run-level STATE. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; -y means dont ask user to confirm shutdown after grace period. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; sleep - Pause program for n seconds &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; sort - Sort file or pipeline &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Usage: sort options [list-of-files] &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Multiple files are merged before sorting. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Std input: Only used if dash (-) is in the list-of-files or no list-of-files is given &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Std output: Used to display results &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; SEE ALSO &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ![sarrow.gif](content/ad91af06ad96c57f0a338bded4c42f0e.gif)*For more information, see pages 202, 223, and 259* &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Useful options: &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Initial options apply to all sort keys. Options following a sort key apply only to that key. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; -b means ignore leading blanks in sort field. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; SEE ALSO &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ![sarrow.gif](content/ad91af06ad96c57f0a338bded4c42f0e.gif)*For more information, see page 204* &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; -d means ignore leading punctuation. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; SEE ALSO &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ![sarrow.gif](content/ad91af06ad96c57f0a338bded4c42f0e.gif)*For more information, see page 208* &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; -f means fold upper/lowercase together. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; SEE ALSO &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ![sarrow.gif](content/ad91af06ad96c57f0a338bded4c42f0e.gif)*For more information, see page 207* &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; -k means define sort keys using new method: -k m opts, n. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; SEE ALSO &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ![sarrow.gif](content/ad91af06ad96c57f0a338bded4c42f0e.gif)*For more information, see page 210* &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; -n means sort numbers by magnitude. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; SEE ALSO &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ![sarrow.gif](content/ad91af06ad96c57f0a338bded4c42f0e.gif)*For more information, see page 204* &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; -o means save output in following filename. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;

 |

&#124; Page 791 &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; SEE ALSO &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ![sarrow.gif](content/ad91af06ad96c57f0a338bded4c42f0e.gif)*For more information, see page 206* &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; -r means sort in reverse order. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; SEE ALSO &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ![sarrow.gif](content/ad91af06ad96c57f0a338bded4c42f0e.gif)*For more information, see pages 207, 259* &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; +m means skip m fields per line and then start sorting. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; SEE ALSO &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ![sarrow.gif](content/ad91af06ad96c57f0a338bded4c42f0e.gif)*For more information, see pages 209, 259* &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; +m options -n defines sort keys within the line. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; SEE ALSO &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ![sarrow.gif](content/ad91af06ad96c57f0a338bded4c42f0e.gif)*For more information, see page 210* &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; split - Split file into smaller files of equal lines &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Usage: split options [filename] [prefix] &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Smaller files will be prefixaa, prefixab, prefixac, and so on. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Std input: Only used if no filename given or dash (-) given as filename &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Std output: Not used &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; SEE ALSO &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ![sarrow.gif](content/ad91af06ad96c57f0a338bded4c42f0e.gif)*For more information, see page 226* &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Useful options: &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; -N creates smaller files of N lines each (except the last one). The default is 1000. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; strings - Show printable strings within any type of file &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Usage: strings options [list-of-files] &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Std input: Only used if no list-of-files is given &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Std output: Used to display results &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; SEE ALSO &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ![sarrow.gif](content/ad91af06ad96c57f0a338bded4c42f0e.gif)*For more information, see page 165* &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Useful options: &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; -n LEN means set min LEN printable sequence to report. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; stty - Set/display terminal characteristics &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

 |

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;

 |

&#124; Page 792 &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Useful command options: &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; -a means show all stty options, precede with minus sign (-) if turned off. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Useful stty options: &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; erase means set/show the erase key. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; SEE ALSO &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ![sarrow.gif](content/ad91af06ad96c57f0a338bded4c42f0e.gif)*For more information, see page 103* &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; intr means set/show the interrupt key. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; SEE ALSO &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ![sarrow.gif](content/ad91af06ad96c57f0a338bded4c42f0e.gif)*For more information, see page 111* &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; tostop means suspend running background jobs when they start any output. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; SEE ALSO &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ![sarrow.gif](content/ad91af06ad96c57f0a338bded4c42f0e.gif)*For more information, see page 325* &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; su - Become superuser or another user &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; sum - Compute checksum on file or pipeline &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Usage: sum options [list-of-files] &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Std input: Only used if no list-of-files is given &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Std output: Used to display results &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Notes: Matching checksum indicates a high probability that the data is the same. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; SEE ALSO &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ![sarrow.gif](content/ad91af06ad96c57f0a338bded4c42f0e.gif)*For more information, see pages 267, 269* &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Useful options: &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; -r means compute rotating checksum that can detect differences in order as well as contents. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; SEE ALSO &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ![sarrow.gif](content/ad91af06ad96c57f0a338bded4c42f0e.gif)*For more information, see pages 267, 269* &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; tail - Display the last lines of a file or pipeline &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Usage: tail options [filename] &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Std input: Only used if no filename is given &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

 |

|  

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;

 |
|  

&#124; Page 793 &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Std output: Used to display results &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; SEE ALSO &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ![sarrow.gif](content/ad91af06ad96c57f0a338bded4c42f0e.gif)*For more information, see page 216* &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Useful options: &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; -f means followthat is, continuously display any data appended to file until Enter key is pressed. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; -n means display just n lines. (Warning: Large values of n can be ignored.) &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; +n means display from line n to end of file. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; tape - Issue magnetic tape commands &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Usage: tape cmd /dev/XXX? &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Std input: Not used &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Std ouput: Not used &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; See the mt command. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; SEE ALSO &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ![sarrow.gif](content/ad91af06ad96c57f0a338bded4c42f0e.gif)*For more information, see page 336* &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Useful commands: &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; rewind 
reten &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; tar - Tape archive &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; SEE ALSO &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ![sarrow.gif](content/ad91af06ad96c57f0a338bded4c42f0e.gif)*For more information, see page 340* &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Useful options when backing up: &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; c means create backup (must be the first option). &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; b means set tape block size. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; f means specify the backup device or file. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; h means follow symbolic links (AIX). &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; L means follow symbolic links (SCO). &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; v means verbose. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

 |

|  

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;

 |
|  

&#124; Page 794 &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Useful options when restoring: &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; x means extract files from backup (must be the first option). &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; A means suppress leading slash in filenames (SCO). &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; m means set date of last modification to when restore was done, else set last mod of original tape files. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; v means verbose. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; tee - Save Std input to file and send same information out std output &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Usage: cmd &#124; tee filename &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Std input: Used to read input &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Std output: Used to display current output &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; SEE ALSO &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ![sarrow.gif](content/ad91af06ad96c57f0a338bded4c42f0e.gif)*For more information, see page 116* &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Useful options: &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; -a means append to file, not overwrite. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; test - Evaluate condition as true or false &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Usage: test condition &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; or: &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; [ condition ] &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; File tests: &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; -f name means is name a regular file? &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; -d name means is name a directory? &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; -r name means is name readable? &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; -w name means is name writable? &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; -x name means is name executable? &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; -c name means is name a char device file? &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; -b name means is name a block device file? &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; -s name means is name a file with size > zero? &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

 |

|  

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;

 |
|  

&#124; Page 795 &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; -h or -L name means is name a symbolic link? &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; String tests: &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; "string" means is string not empty? &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; -z string means is string empty (zero size)? &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; s1 = s2 means are the two strings the same? &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; s1 != s2 means are the two strings not the same? &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Numeric tests: &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; v1 -eq v2 means is v1 equal to v2? &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; We can also test -ne, -gt, -ge, -lt, -le. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Combining tests: &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; -a means logical AND. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; -o means logical OR. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; touch - Update file last access and last modification date/time &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Will create an empty file if it does not exist, but wontaffect the contents of an already existing file. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; tr - Translate characters &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Usage: tr "list1" "list2" < file1 > file 2 &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Std input: Always used, will not accept filenames &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Std output: Used to display results &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Notes: If char is found in list1, replace it with corresponding char in list2. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; SEE ALSO &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ![sarrow.gif](content/ad91af06ad96c57f0a338bded4c42f0e.gif)*For more information, see page 441* &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Useful options: &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; -d means delete the chars found in list 1. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Useful examples: &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; tr "[A-Z]" "[a-z]" # convert upper to lower case 
tr "[\201-\376]\377" "[\001-\176]\177" < file1 > file2 &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

 |

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;

 |

&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; type - Show full pathname of command &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Usage: type unixcmd &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Std input: Not used &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Std output: Used to display results &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; SEE ALSO &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ![sarrow.gif](content/ad91af06ad96c57f0a338bded4c42f0e.gif)*For more information, see page 100* &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Notes: Works in both the Bourne shell and Korn shell &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; tty - Display your current system tty port name &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; umask - Show your current file creation permission mask &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; uname - Display the system type and name &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; uniq - Remove non-uniq lines &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Usage: uniq options [list-of-files] &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Std input: Only used if no list-of-files is given &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Std output: Used to display results &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; SEE ALSO &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ![sarrow.gif](content/ad91af06ad96c57f0a338bded4c42f0e.gif)*For more information, see page 445* &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Useful options: &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; -d means show only duplicated lines. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; -u means show only unique lines. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; -c means show count for each line of number of duplicates. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; uucp - UNIX to UNIX copy over serial lines and modems &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; uuencode/uudecode - Transform/restore file to/from printable text &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Usage: uuencode binaryfile destname > textfile &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Std input: Only used if binary file not given &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Std output: Not used &#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ![sarrow.gif](content/ad91af06ad96c57f0a338bded4c42f0e.gif)*For more information, see pages 449, 471* &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Starting vi: &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; vi -r means display files that can be restored. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; view file means run vi in read-only mode. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Colon commands: &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; :abbrev word means new phrase. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; :!cmd means run UNIX cmd in subshell, and then resume vi. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; :f means show current line number and filename. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; :map c string means map char c to string. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; :q! means quit without saving. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; :w means write changes to disk. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; :w file means save in file. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; :wq means write (save changes) and quit. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Colon set modes, abbreviation, and how to put it back: &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; :set autoindent, :set ai, :set noai :set ignorecase, :set ic, :set noic
:set number, :set nu, :set nonu
:set showmode, :set noshowmode &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; :set wrapmargin=10, turn off by setting to zero &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

 |

|  

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;

 |
|  

&#124; Page 798 &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Replacing in Colon mode: &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; !! cmd means replace current line with output of UNIX cmd. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; !'a cmd means apply UNIX command from cursor to mark a. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; !'a sed 's/st1/st2/g' means replace string st1 with string st2 where found from cursor to mark a. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; :%! sed 's/st1/st2/g' means replace st1 throughout the file. st1 may contain regular expression wildcards. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Copy and paste, and delete and paste: &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; y'a means yank to start of line that contains mark a. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; y`a means yank to mark a. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; y... means follow y with a motion command to indicate how much text to yank and save. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; "ay... means yank and save in named buffer a. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; p means paste unnamed buffer at the current cursor. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; "ap means paste named buffer at the current cursor. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; "np means paste what you deleted n times ago. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Delete text commands: &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; dd means delete line. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; x means delete character. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; D means delete to end of line. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; d'a means delete to start of line that contains mark a. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; d`a means delete to mark a. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; d... means follow d with a motion command to indicate what to delete. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; "ad... means delete and save in named buffer a. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Insert text commnds: &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; i means insert at or left of cursor until Esc. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; I means insert at start of line until Esc. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; a means insert after cursor until Esc. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

 |

|  

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;

 |
|  

&#124; Page 799 &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; A means insert at end of line until Esc. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; o means open line below and insert until Esc. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; O means open line above and insert until Esc. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Miscellaneous commands: &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; J means join lines; nJ joins n lines. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Most vi commands allow a preceding repeat count. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; u means undo last insert/delete/modify. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; U means restore line to when you first got there. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; . means repeat last insert/delete/change. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Modifying text: &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; C means change to end of line with input until Esc. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; CC means change current line until Esc. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; r means replace character. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; R means replace until Esc. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Moving the cursor &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; 0,^,$ mean start of line, first printable char, end of line. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; h,j,k,l mean same as left, down, up, right arrow. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; H,M,L mean move high, medium, low on the current screen. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Gn means go to line n; G means go to end of file. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Ctrl+F/Ctrl+B forward/backward one full screen. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Ctrl+D/Ctrl+U down/up one half screen. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; W,B,E mean move a word ahead, back, or to end of word. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; w,b,e same as preceding explanation, but go to next contained word or non-word. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; mc means set mark c. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; 'c means go to start of line containing mark c. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; `c means go to mark c. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

 |

|  

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;

 |
|  

&#124; Page 800 &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Searching: &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; /string means move ahead to next occurrence of string. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ?string means move back to string. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Regular Expressions are allowed. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; / or ? without a string repeat last search. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; n or N also repeat preceding search. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; fc means move to character c. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ; means repeat preceding f command. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; % means find matching closure symbolfor example [{( )}]. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; whence - Show full pathname of command &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Usage: whence unixcmd &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Std input: Not used &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Std output: Used to display results &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; SEE ALSO &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ![sarrow.gif](content/ad91af06ad96c57f0a338bded4c42f0e.gif)*For more information, see page 100* &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Notes: Works in the Korn shell, but not Bourne shell. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; which - Show full pathname of command &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Usage: which unixcmd &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Std input: Not used &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Std output: Used to display results &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; SEE ALSO &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ![sarrow.gif](content/ad91af06ad96c57f0a338bded4c42f0e.gif)*For more information, see page 100* &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Notes: Works in the Bourne shell, but not Korn shell. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; who - Display who is on the system and other system information &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Usage: who options &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Std output: Used to display results &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124; Page 801 &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Useful options: &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; -b means show date/time of last system reboot. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; -r means show current run-level and when entered. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; SEE ALSO &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ![sarrow.gif](content/ad91af06ad96c57f0a338bded4c42f0e.gif)*For more information, see page 299* &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; wildcard - Filename generation &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; SEE ALSO &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ![sarrow.gif](content/ad91af06ad96c57f0a338bded4c42f0e.gif)*For more information, see page 232* &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; * means zero or more of any character except slash (/) and leading period. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; SEE ALSO &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ![sarrow.gif](content/ad91af06ad96c57f0a338bded4c42f0e.gif)*For more information, see page 232* &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Contain a Pattern (*) &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ? means exactly one of any character except slash (/) and leading period. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; SEE ALSO &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ![sarrow.gif](content/ad91af06ad96c57f0a338bded4c42f0e.gif)*For more information, see page 239* &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Positions (?) &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; [...] means exactly one of the alternatives listed except (/) and leading period. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; SEE ALSO &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ![sarrow.gif](content/ad91af06ad96c57f0a338bded4c42f0e.gif)*For more information, see page 241* &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; [!...] means any one character except for the alternatives listed, cannot match a slash (/) or leading period. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; SEE ALSO &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ![sarrow.gif](content/ad91af06ad96c57f0a338bded4c42f0e.gif)*For more information, see page 243* &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Positions ([!...]) &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; wildcard - Regular expressions (R.E.) &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; SEE ALSO &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ![sarrow.gif](content/ad91af06ad96c57f0a338bded4c42f0e.gif)*For more information, see page 388* &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ^ if at start of pattern indicates start of line. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

 |

|  

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;

 |
|  

&#124; Page 802 &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; SEE ALSO &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ![sarrow.gif](content/ad91af06ad96c57f0a338bded4c42f0e.gif)*For more information, see page 389* &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; $ if at end of pattern indicates end of line. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; SEE ALSO &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ![sarrow.gif](content/ad91af06ad96c57f0a338bded4c42f0e.gif)*For more information, see page 390* &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; . means exactly one of any character. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; SEE ALSO &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ![sarrow.gif](content/ad91af06ad96c57f0a338bded4c42f0e.gif)*For more information, see page 395* &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; [...] means exactly one of the alternatives listed. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; SEE ALSO &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ![sarrow.gif](content/ad91af06ad96c57f0a338bded4c42f0e.gif)*For more information, see page 396* &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; [^...] means any one character except for the alternatives listed. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; SEE ALSO &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ![sarrow.gif](content/ad91af06ad96c57f0a338bded4c42f0e.gif)*For more information, see page 397* &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; \{n\} means exactly n occurrences of preceding element (supported in grep and sed, not supported in egrep or awkuse {n} for Perl). &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; SEE ALSO &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ![sarrow.gif](content/ad91af06ad96c57f0a338bded4c42f0e.gif)*For more information, see page 398* &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; \{n,\} means n or more occurences of preceding element (supported in grep and sed, not supported in egrep or awkuse {n,} for Perl). &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; SEE ALSO &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ![sarrow.gif](content/ad91af06ad96c57f0a338bded4c42f0e.gif)*For more information, see page 398* &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; \{n,m\} means between n and m (inclusive) occurences of preceding element (supported in grep and sed, not supported in egrep or awkuse {n,m} for Perl). &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; SEE ALSO &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ![sarrow.gif](content/ad91af06ad96c57f0a338bded4c42f0e.gif)*For more information, see page 398* &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; * means 0 or more occurrences of preceding element. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; SEE ALSO &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ![sarrow.gif](content/ad91af06ad96c57f0a338bded4c42f0e.gif)*For more information, see page 399* &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; It matches longest possible span. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

 |

|  

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;

 |
|  

&#124; Page 803 &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; SEE ALSO &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ![sarrow.gif](content/ad91af06ad96c57f0a338bded4c42f0e.gif)*For more information, see page 424* &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; *? matches shortest posssible span (perl only). &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; SEE ALSO &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ![sarrow.gif](content/ad91af06ad96c57f0a338bded4c42f0e.gif)*For more information, see page 426* &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; .* means 0 or more occurrences of any character. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; This is just one example of the * wildcard. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; + means 1 or more occurrences of preceding element (supported in egrep, perl, and awk, not supported in grep and sed). &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; SEE ALSO &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ![sarrow.gif](content/ad91af06ad96c57f0a338bded4c42f0e.gif)*For more information, see page 403* &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Matches longest possible span. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; SEE ALSO &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ![sarrow.gif](content/ad91af06ad96c57f0a338bded4c42f0e.gif)*For more information, see page 424* &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; +? matches shortest posssible span (perl only). &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; SEE ALSO &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ![sarrow.gif](content/ad91af06ad96c57f0a338bded4c42f0e.gif)*For more information, see page 426* &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ? means 0 or 1 occurences of preceding element (supported in egrep, perl, and awk, not supported in grep and sed). &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; SEE ALSO &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ![sarrow.gif](content/ad91af06ad96c57f0a338bded4c42f0e.gif)*For more information, see page 403* &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; &#124; allows specifying alternative patterns to search for (supported in egrep, perl, and awk, not supported in grep and sed). &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; SEE ALSO &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ![sarrow.gif](content/ad91af06ad96c57f0a338bded4c42f0e.gif)*For more information, see page 403* &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ( ) allows grouping alternatives (supported in egrep, perl, and awk, not supported in grep and sed). &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; SEE ALSO &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ![sarrow.gif](content/ad91af06ad96c57f0a338bded4c42f0e.gif)*For more information, see page 403* &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; \( \) remembers what characters matched the enclosed pattern (supported in grep and sed, not supported in egrep or awkuse ( ) for perl). &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;

&#124; Page 804 &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; \1, \2 refers to remembered string 1 or 2\. See \( \). &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; \b indicates word boundary (perl only). &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; SEE ALSO &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ![sarrow.gif](content/ad91af06ad96c57f0a338bded4c42f0e.gif)*For more information, see page 405* &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; \B indicates non-word boundary (perl only). &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; SEE ALSO &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ![sarrow.gif](content/ad91af06ad96c57f0a338bded4c42f0e.gif)*For more information, see page 405* &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; \X put backslash (\) before any wildcard X to use it as a literal character in the string. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; xargs - Execute another UNIX command with passed arguments &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Usage: xargs cmd [opts] &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Std input: Used to pass a list of arguments for cmd &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Std output: However cmd uses it &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; SEE ALSO &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ![sarrow.gif](content/ad91af06ad96c57f0a338bded4c42f0e.gif)*For more information, see page 247* &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Useful options: &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; -n NUMB means limit number of arguments put on each tovalue specified as NUMB. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; /dev/null file The place to send output that you are not interesting in seeing; also the place to get input from when you have none (but the program or command requires something). This is also known as the bit bucket (where old bits go to die). &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124; ![fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif](content/fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif) &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; /dev Device directory. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124; ![fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif](content/fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif) &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; /etc/group file This file contains information about groups, the users they contain, and passwords required for access by other users. The password might actually be in another file, the shadow group file, to protect it from attacks. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124; ![fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif](content/fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif) &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; /etc/inittab file The file that contains a list of active terminal ports for which UNIX will issue the logon prompt. This also contains a list of background processes for UNIX to initialize. Some versions of UNIX use other files, such as /etc/tty. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124; ![fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif](content/fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif) &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; /etc/motd file Message of the day file; usually contains information the system administrator feels is important for you to know. This file displays when the user signs on to the system. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;

&#124; ![fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif](content/fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif) &#124;  &#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124; A &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124; ![fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif](content/fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif) &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Absolute pathname is a method of referring to a file where all directories from the root directory to that file are specified. An absolute pathname always starts with a slash, indicating it is starting from root (for example, /reports/abc refers to the abc file in the reports subdirectory of root). &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124; ![fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif](content/fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif) &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Administrative control of a directory Users who have write permission to a directory have effective administrative control over that directory. In addition to creating files, they can delete and rename files of other users, even if they dont have permission to modify those files. If the directory sticky bit is set, having write permission does not give administrative control of the directory. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124; ![fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif](content/fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif) &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; ANSI American National Standards Institute. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124; ![fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif](content/fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif) &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; API Application Program Interface. The specific method prescribed by a computer operating system, application, or third-party tool by which a programmer writing an application program can make requests of the operating system. Also known as Application Programmers Interface. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124; ![fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif](content/fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif) &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Application data file A file, usually one of many, that contains data for that application. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124; ![fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif](content/fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif) &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Application program A software program, usually one of a great many, that provides part of the programming for an application. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124; ![fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif](content/fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif) &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Application One or more software programs that provide a capability, such as an accounting application. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124; ![fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif](content/fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif) &#124;  &#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124; ASCII American Standard Code for Information Interchange. Used to represent characters in memory for most computers. &#124;  &#124;

&#124; ![fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif](content/fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif) &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; AT&T UNIX Original version of UNIX developed at AT&T Bell Labs, later known as UNIX Systems Laboratories. Many current versions of UNIX are descendants; even BSD UNIX was derived from early AT&T UNIX. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124; ![fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif](content/fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif) &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; awk Programming language developed by A.V. Aho, P.J. Weinberger, and Brian W. Kernighan. The language is built on C syntax, includes the regular expression search facilities of grep, and adds in the advanced string and array handling features missing from the C language. nawk, gawk, and POSIX awk are versions of this language. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124; Background job is a job that you initiated but is running independently of your keyboard and screen so that you can do other things. Many important UNIX system processes run as background jobs, waiting for user requests or other &#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Basename The longest right-hand part of a pathname that contains no slashes (/) (for example, in /usr/fred/reports/acme, acme is the basename of that pathname). A basename can be any type of file including a directory. Also basename, as used in this book, can refer to a filename that has no slashes and no directory portion. &#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Bash Stands for GNU Bourne Again Shell and contains most Bourne shell, sh, and Korn shell, ksh, enhancements. &#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Bourne shell A standard shell on all UNIX systems that supports basic programming but few user keyboard conveniences. &#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;

&#124; ![fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif](content/fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif) &#124;  &#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124; C shell A user interface for UNIX written by Bill Joy at Berkeley. It features C programming-like syntax. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124; ![fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif](content/fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif) &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; C Programming language developed by Brian W. Kernighan and Dennis M. Ritchie. The C language is highly portable and available on many platforms including mainframes, PCs, and, of course, UNIX systems. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124; CAD Computer-aided design. &#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;

&#124; ![fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif](content/fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif) &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Cast Programming construct to force type conversion. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124; ![fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif](content/fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif) &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; CD-ROM Compact disc-read only memory. Computer-readable data stored on the same physical form as a musical CD. Large capacity, inexpensive, slower than a hard disk, and limited to reading. There are versions that are writable (CD-R, CD Recordable) and other formats that can be written to once or many times. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124; ![fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif](content/fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif) &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; CGI Common gateway interface. A means of transmitting data between Web pages and programs or scripts executing on the server. Those programs can then process the data and send the results back to the users browser through dynamically creating HTML. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124; ![fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif](content/fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif) &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Character special A device file used to communicate with character-oriented I/O devices such as terminals, printers, or network communications lines. All I/O access is treated as a series of bytes (characters). &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124; ![fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif](content/fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif) &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Characters, alphabetic The letters *A* through *Z* and *a* through *z*. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124; ![fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif](content/fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif) &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Characters, alphanumeric The letters *A* through *Z* and *a* through *z,* the numbers 0 through 9. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124; ![fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif](content/fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif) &#124;  &#124;  &#124;

&#124; ![fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif](content/fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif) &#124;  &#124;  &#124;

&#124; ![fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif](content/fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif) &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Checksum A numeric value produced by summing all the characters within a file. This sum enables you to do a quick check that the file matches another file. By comparing the checksums, you can quickly check whether two files (are likely to) contain the same contents or whether a file still has the same contents it had when the checksum was last computed. Often the sum is shifted or rotated after each character is added (think of multiplying by two). This is then called a rotating checksum, which can detect file differences where the data is the same but in a different order. The goal of the checksum is that a small difference between two files should generate a large difference between the checksums. If two files have the same checksum, there is a high probability that they contain the same contents. If their checksums differ, the two files are definitely not the same. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124; ![fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif](content/fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif) &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Child directory Same as a subdirectory. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124; ![fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif](content/fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif) &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Child process A process or job started by another process or job which is called the parent process. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124; ![fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif](content/fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif) &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Child process See *Subprocess*. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124; ![fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif](content/fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif) &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Child shell See *Subshell*. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124; ![fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif](content/fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif) &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Class A model of objects that have attributes (data) and behavior (code or functions). It is also viewed as a collection of objects in their abstracted form. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124; ![fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif](content/fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif) &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Command substitution A shell feature that allows backquotes (`) containing another UNIX command to substitute the output of that command as words in the current command. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124; ![fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif](content/fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif) &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Command-line editing UNIX shells support the capability to recall a previously entered command, modify it, and then execute the new version. The command history can remain between sessions. (The commands you did yesterday can be available for you when you log on today.) Some shells support a command-line editing mode that uses a subset of the vi, emacs, or gmacs editor commands for command recall and modification. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124; ![fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif](content/fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif) &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Command-line history See *Command-line editing*. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124; ![fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif](content/fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif) &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Command-line parameters Used to specify parameters to pass to the execute program or procedure. Also known as command-line arguments. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124; ![fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif](content/fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif) &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Comment Explanatory words meant for a human reader. Usually comments have special starting characters so that the computer will ignore them. In UNIX shell programming, use a pound sign (#) to start a comment. Other programming languages can use other starting characters for comments. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124; ![fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif](content/fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif) &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Configuration files Collections of information used to initialize and set up the environment for specific commands and programs. Shell configuration files set up the users environment. &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124; ![fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif](content/fc4f3a8aef38b56941e55505c60e4caf.gif) &#124;  &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124; Contained words In vi, contained words are any groups of letters and digits. They are separated from other contained words by punctuation, spaces, tabs, and end of line. For example, &#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;
&#124;  &#124;

&#124;  &#124;  &#124;
